title: Longitudinal records supported forecasts of multiple sclerosis progression
summary: The study used routine records from 1,624 people with multiple sclerosis to forecast transition from relapsing-remitting to secondary-progressive disease at 180, 360 and 720 days. Visit-based models had 70–100% recall but 5–10% precision without confidence filtering; the history model reached 67% recall and 42% precision at 720 days. Few transitions and false positives limit treatment use; the study does not show clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Recurrent neural network (LSTM); random forest, SVM, KNN and AdaBoost
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; IRCCS Istituto Neurologico Mediterraneo Neuromed

evidence.tested: A single-center retrospective cohort of 18,574 visits from 1,624 patients. Visit models used patient-wise leave-one-group-out evaluation; the history model used a train/test split because leave-one-group-out training was computationally infeasible.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: The models learned from clinical visits or longitudinal patient history to forecast disease-course transition.
